body.title: [ci] perf: speed up full-repository Biome checks
body.body:
## Description

The goal of this PR is to speedup formatting in the CI. It has grown to become very slow, growing to more than 8 minutes.

After profiling what takes the most time and what could be sped up, it turns out that repeated Grit syntax-tree matching takes most of the time.
This PR adds source-text prefilters to the most expensive plugins and substring guards before the regex checks, which will be faster for the exact same check.

Local wall times on main: `format:ci` 37.6s → 17.4s, `format` 117.3s → 44.1s.

Commands to run to profile the formatting:

```bash
biome ci --error-on-warnings .
biome ci --error-on-warnings --skip=suspicious/noImportCycles .
biome ci --error-on-warnings --skip=plugin .
biome ci --error-on-warnings --linter-enabled=false --assist-enabled=false .

biome ci --error-on-warnings . \
  --log-level=tracing \
  --log-kind=json \
  --log-file=/tmp/speedup-biome-trace.json
```

## Tests

- Existing Grit samples passed; 150 before/after fixture cases produced identical diagnostics, including repeated violations, escaped spellings, templates, JSX text, and suppressions.
- Tested both full-repository commands locally.

## Risk

- Low.

## Deploy Plan

- No deploy.

body.title: [front] Keep the caller's key scope on system-key sub-agent calls
body.body:
## Description

Stacked on #33926 (the acting user comes from the credential; it also holds the stack overview).

`run_agent`, `agent_router` and `run_dust_app` call the public API again with the workspace system key. Without a user to impersonate (a conversation driven by a regular API key), that call carried only the role, so it ran with every group of the system key and could reach spaces and agents the key was never scoped to. A shared `getSystemKeyReentryHeaders` helper now builds these headers for all three: the user's email when there is one, otherwise the calling key's own groups in `X-Dust-Group-Ids`, plus the role and attribution key name.

`agent_router` now also forwards the role, like `run_agent` already did, so a user's agent list reflects their real role (capped by their membership). An empty group list throws instead of being sent, since the API reads an empty header as "no restriction".

Cards: dust-tt/tasks#10774, dust-tt/tasks#10809. `run_dust_app` had the same hole and gets the same fix. No visual change.

## Tests

* Round trip through `publicApiAuth`: headers built from a userless regular key resolve to that key's groups and role on the system key, not to a restricted group the key lacks. This test fails without the group forwarding.
* Headers built from a user's auth still resolve to that user.
* Ran the `run_agent`, `run_dust_app`, `agent_router` and MCP action suites (156 passed) and the `front-api` middleware and v1 assistant suites (113 passed).

## Risk

Low. Only sub-agent, agent-router and Dust app calls from userless (API-key) conversations change: they now see what the key sees. If a key's scope is narrower than an integration assumed, a sub-agent call returns "not available" instead of running. Safe to revert.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy `front` workers after #33926. No migration, no flag.

body.title: [front,connectors] Exclude originating Slack thread from retrieval

labels.name: documentation-ack
labels.description: Used to acknowledge that documentation is up-to-date with this PR

labels.name: sdk-ack
labels.description: Used to acknowledge that you are not breaking the public API.

body.body:
## Description

Fixes https://github.com/dust-tt/tasks/issues/10294

Asked from inside a Slack thread to find an *earlier* thread, the bot returned a link to the **current** thread. The active Slack thread is indexed into the data source with the user's question text verbatim (as a document tagged `threadId:<ts>`), so it self-matches on its own query and gets served back as the answer. Its content is already provided to the conversation as a content fragment, so retrieving the indexed copy only ever hurts.

This adds a generic, channel-agnostic retrieval-scope hint on the user message context: **`excludedRetrievalTags`** — opaque `key:value` tag strings a run asks retrieval to skip (merged into each data source's `filter.tags.not`). The conversation/message models stay entirely Slack-agnostic; the **only** component that knows the Slack→tag mapping is the connectors Slack bot, which sets `excludedRetrievalTags: ["threadId:<threadTs>"]`.

- `sdks/js` + `front` `UserMessageContext`: new optional `excludedRetrievalTags`.
- `front-api`: forwarded on post-message and create-conversation; swagger schemas updated.
- `front`: persisted via new nullable column `userContextExcludedRetrievalTags` on `user_messages` (pre-deploy migration), read back into the message context.
- `front`: both query-based search tools (`search` and `data_sources_file_system/search`) exclude the tags. New `@cc` contract `excluded-retrieval-tags-honored` documents the invariant for future retrieval tools.
- `connectors`: Slack bot stamps the originating thread's tag.

## Tests

- `tsgo --noEmit` clean on front, front-api, connectors; SDK build passes.
- `messages.test.ts` + `conversation/messages.test.ts` — 40/40 pass, exercising the new column's persist→readback roundtrip.
- Biome clean on all changed files.

## Risk

Low. The field is optional everywhere and defaults to no exclusions, so non-Slack runs are unaffected. The exclusion is applied post-`checkConflictingTags` at `finalTagsNot`, and the tags only exist on documents that carry them, so excluding them on other data sources is a no-op. Safe to roll back (additive nullable column, expand-only).

## Deploy Plan

1. Run the pre-deploy migration `20260907175148_add_excluded_retrieval_tags_to_user_messages.sql` (adds nullable column) **before** deploying code.
2. Deploy front / front-api / connectors (rebuilt `@dust-tt/client` is bundled via the workspace file dependency). Field is optional in all directions, so relative deploy order does not matter.

body.title: [front] Only authenticated authors can steer a running agent loop
body.body:
Fixes GHSA-p4m7-q23x-fvrh (tracking: https://github.com/dust-tt/tasks/issues/10755).

## Description

A regular API key has no user, so `postUserMessage` resolves the message author from the caller-supplied `context.email`. When an agent loop is running, a message mentioning that agent is stored as `pending` (steering). When the loop ends, `updateAgentMessageWithFinalStatus` promotes it and builds `Authenticator.fromUserIdAndWorkspaceId` for its author, so the next agent run executes with the attributed member's role, groups and personal MCP connections. A pending message with no author similarly runs with the authority of the loop it steers.

This PR only lets a message go `pending` when `auth` is a system key (already trusted to impersonate via `x-api-user-email`), or `auth` has a user and the message's author is that user or nobody. Other callers (regular API keys, user-less sandbox tokens) get a visible message answered by their own agent loop, with their own authority. Adds the `steering-requires-authenticated-author` contract on `postUserMessage`.

Display attribution through `context.email` is intentionally unchanged: removing it for non-system callers breaks customer workflows and needs a deprecation process.

Behavior change: a regular API key posting while its agent runs now gets a parallel answer instead of interrupting and redirecting the running loop. Connectors (system keys with `x-api-user-email`) keep steering.

## Tests

New `postUserMessage` tests in `conversation.test.ts`: a session user still steers; an API key attributing a member by email gets its own loop with a user-less auth while the message stays attributed; an unattributed API key message doesn't steer. The two API-key tests fail without the fix. Full file passes (92 tests).

## Risk

Low. Only affects messages posted by user-less, non-system callers while an agent loop is running in the conversation.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy `front`.

body.title: [connectors] Bind Firecrawl webhook events to the connector's current crawl
body.body:
## Description

Fixes dust-tt/tasks#10794. The Firecrawl webhook trusted the body's `connectorId` and crawl `id` behind only the shared webhook URL secret, so a forged `crawl.started` + `crawl.completed` could wipe any tenant's webcrawler data source via GC (or `crawl.page` could inject content). Events are now ignored unless `id` matches the connector's stored `crawlId`, and GC no longer runs when the crawl status check fails for a reason other than job expiry.

## Tests

New `webhook_firecrawl.test.ts` (fails on the old handler); tsgo + biome clean.

## Risk

Page webhooks arriving after the `crawl.completed` activity clears `crawlId` are now dropped (then GC'd until next crawl). Monitor the new "Webhook does not match the connector's current crawl" warning. No workflow code change.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy connectors.

body.title: [front] chore: verify WorkOS tokens with jose and drop jwks-rsa
body.body:
## Description

Stacked on #33932 (invitation tokens on jose).

WorkOS bearer tokens were verified with `jsonwebtoken` plus `jwks-rsa`. `verifyWorkOSToken` now uses jose's `jwtVerify` with `createRemoteJWKSet`, still RS256 and the same issuer check. `jwks-rsa` is removed from front and from the front-api bundled-deps allowlist.

Two things to look at. The old code created a new `jwks-rsa` client on every call, so its cache never helped. The key set is now created once per process, and jose caches it. Expired-token detection in `getSessionFromBearerToken` now checks jose's `JWTExpired`, which jose only throws after the signature checks out, so the meaning is the same. Dropping `jsonwebtoken`'s `any` claim type surfaced one loose read: `org_id` is now kept only when it is a string.

No visual change.

## Tests

* New `verifyWorkOSToken` tests against a local RSA key set: valid token, expired (returns `JWTExpired`), wrong issuer, unknown key.
* Ran `npm run test` on workos, auth and mcp_server in front plus the front-api middlewares (118 passed), and `npm run tsgo` and `check:bundled-deps` locally.

## Risk

Medium. This is the bearer-token login path for the extension and API clients. If it is wrong, those clients get 401s, or an expired token is no longer reported as `expired_oauth_token_error`. Rollback is a revert.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy after #33932. front-api. No migration, no flag.

body.title: [front] chore: sign and verify invitation tokens with jose
body.body:
## Description

Stacked on #33931 (viz tokens on jose).

Membership invitation tokens now use the jose helper. `getMembershipInvitationToken` and `getMembershipInvitationUrl` become async. The routes that mint one token per pending invitation (`/invitations`, `/me/pending-invitations`, cell lookup, poke memberships) now use `concurrentExecutor` instead of `.map`, per the `Promise.all` rule.

Invitations live up to 7 days, so tokens signed by `jsonwebtoken` are still around. They keep working: same secret, same HS256 signature, same `iat`/`exp`. The helper test in #33930 checks this with a fixed legacy token. Verification now accepts only HS256. Before, any HMAC algorithm was accepted, but we only ever signed with HS256.

No visual change.

## Tests

* Invitation reminder tests (token anchoring and expiry) ported to jose.
* Ran `npm run test` on invitation reminders, signup, join and the invitation routes (38 passed) and `npm run tsgo` in front and front-api locally.

## Risk

Low. If this is wrong, invite links would be rejected as invalid on join. Rollback is a revert.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy after #33931. front-api and front workers (reminder emails). No migration, no flag.

Viz access tokens (used by Frames, PDF export and screenshots) still use `jsonwebtoken`. They now go through the shared jose helper. `generateVizAccessToken` and `extractAndVerifyVizAccessTokenFromHeader` become async, and the three `/v1/viz` routes plus the public frame route, PDF export and screenshot await them. body.title: [front] chore: sign and verify sandbox and egress tokens with jose
body.body:
## Description

First of 5 PRs moving our JWT code from `jsonwebtoken` + `jwks-rsa` to `jose`, which we already use and which handles signing, verifying and remote key sets on its own. `jsonwebtoken` is barely maintained and has a history of security advisories.

This PR adds a small `signHS256Jwt` / `verifyHS256Jwt` helper in `lib/utils/hs256_jwt.ts` and moves sandbox exec tokens and egress proxy tokens to it. Token format does not change: HS256, same claims, `typ: JWT`, `iat` and `exp` set as before. The one design choice: jose's sign and verify are async, so `mintEgressJwt` and `mintEgressInvalidationJwt` now return promises and their callers await them. The helper imports the secret as a WebCrypto `CryptoKey`, because jose's raw-bytes `instanceof` check fails under the jsdom test environment.

No visual change.

## Tests

* New helper tests: round trip, `iat`/`exp` handling, wrong secret, expiry, rejection of other HMAC algorithms, and a fixed token signed by `jsonwebtoken` that still verifies.
* Existing sandbox access token and egress tests ported to jose.
* Ran `npm run test` on these suites (74 passed) and `npm run tsgo` in front locally.

## Risk

Low. If something is off, sandbox exec calls or egress proxy auth would fail with 401s. The Rust egress proxy verifies standard HS256, which is unchanged. Rollback is a revert.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy front-api and the front workers as usual. No migration, no flag.

body.title: [front] refactor: replace date-fns-tz zone conversions with @date-fns/tz
body.body:
## Description

Stacked on #33916 (formatting moved to `@date-fns/tz`).

The remaining zone conversions move to date-fns v4 `{ in: tz(zone) }` options and `TZDate`, and `date-fns-tz` is removed from `front` and `front-api`. Outlook's `toDate(str, { timeZone })` becomes `parseISO(str, { in: tz(zone) })`, and `dayBoundaryInTimezone` builds a `TZDate` from the calendar fields instead of the strip-the-Z string trick.

Two things to look at. A `TZDate` serializes with its own offset (`...+09:00`), so `daysToInstantRange` and `dayBoundaryInTimezone` convert back to a plain `Date` to keep UTC strings. Where a timezone skips local midnight (Santiago on 2024-09-08), start of day is now 01:00 local, the first real instant of that day, where `date-fns-tz` returned 23:00 the previous evening. No visual change.

## Tests

* The existing suites (timezone, activation slots, observability, workspace analytics, analytics exports) pass locally under `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` and `TZ=Asia/Tokyo`: 261 tests each.
* Old and new `daysToDateRange` / `daysToInstantRange` compared across 6 zones, a year of hourly instants and 3 window sizes: 9 of 24,696 cases differ, all the Santiago skipped midnight above.

## Risk

Low to Medium. This touches the activation nudge scheduler and analytics date windows. A wrong conversion would shift a window or a nudge slot by the zone's offset, which the tests above would catch for the zones covered. Rollback is a revert.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy `front` and `front-api` after #33916. No migration, no flag.

A whitelisted Slack workflow bot has no Dust user to exchange the system key for, so front kept the system key's default `admin` role while narrowing it to the whitelisted groups. Slack requests that send `X-Dust-Group-Ids` now always send `X-Dust-Role: user` too, and a `@cc` contract says they must.

## Tests

Typecheck + Biome. For human Slack users nothing changes: the email exchange already sets their role to `user`, and `lowestRole` caps any requested role at their membership.

## Risk

Low. Bot runs can no longer see agents or do things that only an admin role allows. Users matched by email are unaffected. Safe to roll back.

body.body:

body.title: [front] Route Salesforce attachment downloads through the egress proxy and validate the instance URL host
body.body:
## Description

Fixes dust-tt/tasks#11026.

`read_attachment` downloaded Salesforce attachment bodies with the global `fetch` (lint rule disabled), so requests to the connection's `instance_url` skipped the untrusted egress proxy, followed redirects freely and returned the full body to the agent. The only guard on `instance_url` was a string prefix/suffix check, which `https://evil.example/x.salesforce.com` passes.

- `downloadSalesforceAttachment` / `downloadSalesforceFile` now go through `untrustedFetch`, like the other MCP servers that hit user-configured hosts.
- `isValidSalesforceDomain` parses the URL and requires a bare https origin whose hostname ends with `.salesforce.com`. It gates connection creation in the OAuth provider and the extract-config UI, so jsforce and core can no longer be pointed at a non-Salesforce host.

Not covered here: jsforce (`identity()`, SOQL) and core's token exchange still reach `instance_url` without the egress proxy. Follow-up: pass the proxy via jsforce's `httpProxy` connection option.

## Tests

Unit tests for the validator (bypass variants, trailing slash, path, port, uppercase host, http, non-string). `npm run test -- types/oauth/lib.test.ts` passes.

## Risk

Worst case, an org with an uppercase or `:443` instance URL can no longer create a connection until they fix the input. Existing connections are unaffected. Safe to rollback.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy front.

body.title: Trigger: only allow trigger-estimation for trigger wher the user can read at least one view
body.body:
## Description

Closes https://github.com/dust-tt/tasks/issues/10961

**What was wrong:**
A webhook source (e.g. a GitHub connection) receives events, and their full contents (payloads) are stored. Admins choose which spaces can use a source by adding it to those spaces; each of these placements is called a view. The `trigger-estimation` endpoint answers "out of the last 100 events, how many match this filter?" It only checked that the  caller was in the workspace, not that they had access to any space where the source is available.

So any member could aim it at a source they weren't allowed to see and send filters like "does field X start with a?", then ab, and so on. The count told them whether each guess was right, which let them slowly rebuild the contents of events they shouldn't see.

**The fix**
The endpoint now requires the caller to have access to at least one view of the source. Otherwise it returns "not found", so it doesn't even confirm the source exists.

**Why this is enough**
Anyone with access to a view can already see the full payloads without guessing: they can set up a trigger on an agent with that source, and every event (with its payload) is passed to the agent and shown to them. The estimation endpoint now only answers people who could read the data directly anyway, so counting gives them nothing new.

The UI isn't affected: the trigger editor only calls this endpoint for a view the user can already see.

## Tests

added unit test

## Risk

low

## Deploy Plan

deploy front

body.title: [front] fix: handle cancellation rejections inside heartbeat
body.body:
## Description

We are seeing some unhandled rejections in agnet loop workers around cancelled failures from Temporal ([logs](https://app.datadoghq.eu/logs?query=%40panic%3Atrue%20cell%3Acell-00001&agg_m=count&agg_t=count&event=AwAAAaD7uXQ_b0KZGgAAABhBYUQ3dVhva0FBREIwcllpRVpha3h3Qm0AAAAkMDFhMGZiYjktOWVkNi00ODk3LWJkYTYtZmFmNmY5NGZjY2QxAABDpw&index=%2A&storage=hot&from_ts=1790927841000&to_ts=1790929641000&live=false)).

The `CancelledFailure: CANCELLED` rejections happens in MCP tool heartbeats, we discard the promise from a sleep (we have a `sleep(0)` in our `heartbeat` util function to detect whether the ).

This PR observes failures inside `heartbeat()` so discarded `CancelledFailure` rejections do not trigger unhandled-rejection reporting. It returns the original promise, so awaited cancellation still rejects and stops the caller. Unexpected heartbeat errors are reported with `panic: true` and remain observable by awaited callers.

## Tests

- Tested locally.

## Risk

- Low. Scoped to heartbeat rejection handling.

## Deploy Plan

- Deploy front agent loop workers.

body.title: dfs v1: add SlateDB block storage and cached Linux FUSE client

labels.name: PMRR
labels.description: Add when you PMRR so that z can find them easily

body.body:
## Description

Adds the dfs v1 exploration: a Rust gRPC server and Linux FUSE client with metadata, grant indexes, and all file content stored directly in SlateDB/GCS as 64 KiB blocks.

- Workspace/session authorization, inherited grants, private root and `/shared` projections, stable object IDs, and atomic mutations with per-object version checks.
- SlateDB memory acknowledgements, native WAL persistence, configurable RAM/disk caches, and cold recovery from GCS.
- Kernel metadata/directory/page caching and writeback, targeted local invalidation, and deferred write errors reported by fsync/close. No cache freshness deadline or cross-client invalidation.
- Design, contracts, setup instructions, and both full benchmark tables in [RESULTS.md](https://github.com/dust-tt/dust/blob/spolu/dfs-v1/x/spolu/dfs/v1/bench/RESULTS.md).

With jd's unchanged 10,000-file corpus, untar improved from 84.83 s to 17.08 s, followed by 5.57 s of remaining SlateDB persistence drain. Warm traversal improved from 101.37 s to 0.147 s. Small create/write and fsync timings increased; these are single-run comparisons. The server restarts once before each suite, not between rows.

## Tests

- `cargo test --workspace --locked`: native unit, filesystem, authorization/race, and real gRPC tests passed.
- Linux FUSE tests passed, including two-mount conflicts, cached revocation, partial writes, append/truncate, local invalidation, and deferred unlink/writeback failures.
- Process-crash recovery verified complete recovered operations with local caches discarded.
- GCS benchmark: all 24 workload checks passed; measured remaining client writeback and SlateDB persistence drain separately, then removed the isolated fixture.

## Risk

Low production risk: isolated exploration under `x/spolu/dfs/v1`, with no existing service integration. Fsync promises server visibility, not GCS durability; crashes may lose recent acknowledged writes. Cached data may remain readable after revocation. Single-server ownership and immediate server-side unlink remain deliberate PoC limitations.

## Deploy Plan

No production deployment. Run manually using the v1 README and a fresh GCS prefix; the storage format is separate from v0.
